title: AlphaForgeBench: Benchmarking End-to-End Trading Strategy Design with Large Language Models

task.value: Benchmarking LLMs as quantitative researchers that generate executable alpha factors and factor-based trading strategy code, rather than emitting buy/hold/sell actions directly.
task.quote: Rather than requiring models to emit discrete trading actions, AlphaForgeBench tasks LLMs with generating executable alpha factors and composing factor-based trading strategies grounded in financial domain knowledge.

architecture.value: A generate-and-backtest pipeline. A standardized prompt combines a system instruction, the strategy query and a factor library. The LLM returns a Python generate_signal function, which a deterministic backtest engine executes. Queries come from real-world extraction (via gemini-3-flash-preview) plus LLM-augmented 3x3 difficulty queries.
architecture.quote: The model must return a self-contained Python function (generate_signal) that consumes a dataframe of OHLCV columns and precomputed indicator factors and produces a trading-signal series dictating position actions (e.g., invest versus hold cash).

data.value: Daily OHLCV with precomputed technical indicators for 7 assets: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT from Binance; AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA and TSLA from Yahoo Finance. Queries: 633 real-world single-asset queries plus 270 structured queries.
data.quote: Each generated strategy is executed within the unified backtest engine across 7 assets spanning two distinct market regimes: 2 cryptocurrencies (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT; sourced from Binance) and 5 US equities (AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA, TSLA; sourced from Yahoo Finance).

window.value: 5-year evaluation window from 2021-01-01 to 2026-01-01, with a 300-day lookback; no train/validation split is described. A separate direct-trading instability study used BTC over 01/01/2025–01/01/2026.
window.quote: The evaluation window spans 5 years (2021-01-01 to 2026-01-01), deliberately selected to cover heterogeneous market conditions including bull rallies, bear corrections, AI-driven recoveries, and prolonged consolidation phases

models.value: claude-sonnet-4.5, deepseek-v3.2, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3-pro-preview, gpt-5.2 and grok-4.1-fast, all via official APIs. gemini-3-flash-preview was used for extraction and gpt-5.2 for query generation.
models.quote: We benchmark six frontier LLMs spanning five providers: claude-sonnet-4.5, deepseek-v3.2, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3-pro-preview, gpt-5.2, and grok-4.1-fast.

baselines.value: The LLMs are compared against each other, and the code-generation paradigm is compared against direct-trading (action-emitting) LLM setups.
baselines.quote: The results confirm that AlphaForgeBench offers a significantly more stable and discriminatory assessment of financial capabilities compared to direct-trading baselines.

headline_result.value: On real-world queries over 2021–2026, gemini-3-pro-preview is best: SR 0.449±0.262, ARR 0.171±0.123, MDD 0.174, CR 1.411, SoR 0.767, VOL 0.237. On structured queries it reaches SR 0.628 at T=0.

costs.value: Main text uses a fixed one-way transaction cost of 10^{-3} with no slippage or liquidity modeling. Appendix Table 9 instead lists a transaction cost of 0 (frictionless), so the paper is inconsistent. Inference cost is not quantified.
costs.quote: and a fixed one-way transaction cost of 10^{-3} , thereby isolating intrinsic signal quality from confounding portfolio-construction effects.

uncertainty.value: k=5 independent generations per query, with metrics reported as mean ± std. A temperature ablation compares τ=0 and τ=0.7. Intra-query std is reported as an order of magnitude below inter-query std, and figures show 25th–75th percentile bands.
uncertainty.quote: Every experiment runs k{=}5 independent generations per query to quantify run-to-run variability.

leakage_controls.value: Only for the direct-trading instability study, the most recent window (2025–2026) was chosen to minimize training-data leakage. No contamination control is described for the main 2021–2026 benchmark.
leakage_controls.quote: Notably, we choose the window 01/01/2025–01/01/2026 to minimize data leakage. Some models may have been trained on market data from earlier periods, which would introduce leakage risk; we therefore use the most recent available span.

limitations.value: Scope is limited to single-asset, long-only strategies with a fixed cost and no slippage or liquidity modeling. Results measure strategy design quality, not deployable performance. Stage 2 queries are augmentations rather than broad ecological coverage.
limitations.quote: The current evaluation targets single asset long only strategy design under a standardized backtesting environment with a fixed transaction cost of 10^{-3} and without explicit slippage or liquidity modeling.

release.value: Code and data (query set, pipeline, backtest engine, scripts) are promised publicly upon acceptance. A webpage is at https://finbrain-lab-hkustgz.github.io/AlphaForgeBench.
release.quote: All code and data will be publicly available upon acceptance of this paper, including the benchmark query set, evaluation pipeline, backtest engine, and supplementary scripts for reproducing the reported results.
